supported: Public authoritative/author-associated material recovers the existence, structure and processing provenance of deployed H10/IMS hydroacoustic calibration sequences.
The public material recovers derived H10S fault-era calibration results and the 2013 cross-talk chronology.
The frozen public crawl did not recover actual H10S calibration-sequence sample bytes, a machine-readable numeric H10S transfer-function table, or an actual calibration start/end timestamp table.
The deployed UWS digitizer calibration is not the same object as a full hydrophone+preamp+riser end-to-end calibration.
interpretation.key_bridge: The authoritative fault-era calibration history lives in a provenance lane distinct from EarthScope public StationXML. Public StationXML is static across 2013, while CTBTO-derived calibration material records a fault-era H10S change; therefore public StationXML correction cannot be treated as a complete historical correction of the south-triplet physical measurement chain.

whole_picture_update.instrument_lane: Strengthened: a documented H10S fault/cross-talk history and derived calibration changes are real, but their underlying calibration samples remain unrecovered publicly in this gate and deployed calibration excludes parts of the analogue sensing/riser path.
whole_picture_update.persistent_baseline_lane: Still live: later H10S2/H10N1 broadband scale offset is much larger as an observed cross-station effect than anything this gate can identify one-to-one, and public response correction does not collapse it.
whole_picture_update.older_electronics_watchlist: Separate literature reports H10 data-logger electronic artefacts before 2013, so an early baseline must not be assumed instrument-clean merely because it predates the 2013 H10S1 event.
whole_picture_update.physical_geometry_lane: Unchanged and independent: exact native bathymetry/backscatter/swath evidence is still needed for any claim about a persistent seabed structure.
